today_summary: GCM26 marks $4,396 on the 2026-09-02 chain, $85 (-1.90%) lower, with ATM IV unchanged at 22.69% implying a $63 (1.43%) 1σ session range — $4,333 to $4,459. Yesterday's support void is gone: $4,300 put OI jumped 2,426 → 3,999 (+64.8%) and $4,250 went 1,742 → 2,845 (+63.3%), a combined 2,676 fresh contracts absorbing 3,257 of today's 6,177 put lots. Spot now sits $304 under the $4,700 gamma flip — the deepest short-gamma position of the window — with near-money net GEX (±$200) down to 126.9 from 494.8 five sessions ago. The $5,650 max pain remains untradeable: 37.1% of call OI sits at or above $6,000 in legacy long-dated strikes.
five_day_thesis: Two things have moved in tandem over five sessions: the gamma flip has climbed $4,510 → $4,600 → $4,700 (+$190) while spot fell $4,652.6 → $4,396.0 (-$256.6, -5.51%), widening the short-gamma gap from zero to $304 and leaving dealer hedging pro-cyclical at every price traded this week. The cushion has drained with it — window net GEX 842.3 → 441.4 (-47.6%), near-money net GEX 494.8 → 126.9 (-74.3%) — so the same order flow now moves price roughly four times as far as it did on 08-27. The decisive change today is where the hedges sit: put OI within $500 below spot has built 19,656 → 33,619 (+71.0%), and for the first time in the window the top near-money put wall is no longer the legacy $3,900 strike but $4,300, meaning the demand is real and current rather than decayed inventory. Against that, the upside tail keeps being dismantled — $8,000 call OI 27,026 → 17,760 (-9,266, -34.3%), with -3,253 in this session alone — which is what dragged max pain $6,000 → $5,650 (-$350) and migrated the chain-wide call wall $8,000 → $6,000. ATM IV has compressed 24.60% → 22.69% (-1.91pp) across a 5.5% decline and went flat today, so vol supply is still meeting every downtick: this is a managed, hedged repricing, not a liquidation.

prediction: Bias stays bearish below $4,459 but with reduced conviction — spot is short-gamma under the $4,700 flip, yet it has now arrived at the $4,300–$4,250 shelf where 6,844 contracts of fresh put OI were built. Expect the lower 1σ at $4,333 to be tested and the $4,300 wall to hold on first contact; a clean break below $4,250 re-opens pro-cyclical hedging toward $4,200 (2,452 OI) with nothing structural until $4,000.
